hero.headline: Indian River County schools develop strategy to reverse enrollment decline amid school choice expansion
hero.body:
Indian River County school officials are working to address enrollment declines as school choice options expand across the county. New research examines the district's strategy for competing in the evolving educational landscape.

The case study explores how district administrators are responding to the challenges posed by expanding school choice programs. Indian River County schools face increasing competition as families gain access to more educational alternatives.

School choice programs have grown significantly in Florida in recent years, allowing parents to direct public education dollars toward charter schools, private schools, and other alternatives to traditional public schools. The expansion has forced traditional school districts to adapt their recruitment and retention strategies.

The research highlights Indian River County's approach as officials work to attract and retain students. District leaders are developing new strategies to compete with alternative education providers as enrollment patterns shift across the county.

cards.headline: DEA warns meth surge is hitting Treasure Coast as cocaine prices rise
cards.teaser: Federal agents in Palm Beach County seized about 54 kilos of crystal meth in just two days, part of what they call an unprecedented surge in methamphetamine fueled by the rising cost of cocaine. One DEA agent said the surge is beginning to spread to the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
Federal agents in Palm Beach County are warning of an unprecedented surge in methamphetamine fueled by rising cocaine prices. Inside the DEA's West Palm Beach office, federal agents packed up 12 kilos of pure crystal meth, part of a larger haul of about 54 kilos pulled off Palm Beach County streets in just two days. One seizure was laced with deadly fentanyl. Special Agent Kevin Bobbitt said the scale of what agents are seeing is unlike anything he has encountered in South Florida. The surge is tied directly to economics, as an ounce of cocaine now sells for $600 to $1,000 while an ounce of meth ranges from $280 to $500. A meth lab was recently busted in Palm Beach County, and the surge is beginning to spread to counties in the Treasure Coast, though not yet at the same volume.

Jim and Adrienne Tichy run a halfway house called The Lodge at Delray Beach and have witnessed the surge in meth firsthand and its devastating consequences. According to a 2026 White House report, in some states overdose deaths involving meth have surpassed those from fentanyl. Bobbitt said agents are working aggressively to dismantle the organizations behind the surge. The DEA is urging the public to contact them at 1-877-792-2873 if they see any suspicious activity related to drug trafficking.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
cards.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
cards.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.

cards.headline: 24 immigration arrests conducted in Martin County during federal operation
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement conducted 24 immigration arrests in Martin County on Tuesday, according to data kept by FDLE. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirms FDLE was the agency behind the arrests.

South Florida immigration attorneys are noticing a shift in how federal and local law enforcement are carrying out immigration arrests, with fewer high-profile raids that spark public outrage and raise legal concerns. The change appears to coincide with Markwayne Mullin replacing Kristi Noem as Homeland Security Secretary in March. Renata Castro, an immigration attorney based in Coral Springs, said she has seen the shift firsthand. Castro said she is seeing more detained cases across her desk and a lot more traffic-related detentions resulting in immigration detention. Castro said what occurred during Kristi Noem's term was a lot of arrests without a warrant and just a big spectacle overall. Immigration attorneys previously questioned the legality of many detentions carried out during Noem's tenure. Castro said these are arrests without warrants, but still following the safeguards that the law requires local law enforcement to abide by, and that is why there is an uptick in detention numbers. According to NBC News, ICE arrested 10,000 people over five days this month. WPTV has reached out to ICE and FDLE for comment.

cards.headline: Woman charged with using vehicle to assault three people in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Tioniea Hines, 22, is being held in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond and faces three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.
cards.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, is in St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond, facing three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. Authorities accused her of using a vehicle in a three-person assault.

The charges stem from an incident in which Hines allegedly used her vehicle as a weapon against three individuals. Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon is a felony charge in Florida that carries significant prison time if convicted.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Southeast Region Youth of the Year for the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, will serve as one of 12 club members selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19.
cards.body:
Rosario Liz was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with the once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. Along with the trip, Rosario Liz also received official gear.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. He said he has been forcing his parents to watch every game. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate.

He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. He said the club really helped him to find what his leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what his definition of leadership was. He closed with a message for the younger members of the club looking up to him, telling them to stay with their Boys & Girls Clubs because one day he wants to see each and every one of them in the same position that he is in right now.

cards.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
cards.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top rewards visitors with panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
cards.body:
Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse features a striking red brick tower rising high above the inlet. The 105-step climb takes visitors up a narrow spiral staircase, the same stairs that lighthouse keepers climbed night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners. At the gallery, panoramic views reveal the Atlantic Ocean stretching endlessly to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel, and the sea breeze offers relief on warm Florida mornings.

The museum grounds feature restored historic buildings that tell the story of the lighthouse's past. The site's history spans from its construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. The lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years, standing as a landmark at the base of the Jupiter Inlet.

cards.headline: Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Treasure Coast shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
cards.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they're excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. Cheryl said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. She said they're the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what's on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that.

Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. They said prices are gonna stay inflated and are not gonna go down, adding they'd be willing to bet on that. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. They said having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff in dramatic Wimbledon semifinal tiebreaker
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's Wimbledon run with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that concluded with a drama-filled tiebreaker, becoming the fourth Czech woman in six years to reach the grass-court Grand Slam final.
hero.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova as runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova as champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova as champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon after recovering from five blown match points
cards.teaser: Czech player Linda Noskova captured her first Grand Slam trophy Saturday, defeating Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech Wimbledon final after wasting five match points in the second set.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old Noskova became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, attended the match. Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club, watched from the Royal Box seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who presented the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova.

Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Park Vista football team aims for state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find their footing early in 2025 but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said the team felt good throughout the second half of that season and is working towards being able to carry that through the whole season. Bender said the team has all the pieces in place now and it is just about executing. The program has not achieved a state title since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. Hanna said the Cobras have to handle business weekly and if they do that and do their job, that will get them in the playoffs. Senior Erik Lee said he feels like the team has the guys needed to get it done but they also have to put the work in to get there as well. Senior Justice Jones said it is going to feel amazing because he already knows it is going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school sales tax holiday runs July 20 through August 20 with exemptions on clothing, supplies and computers
cards.teaser: Florida families can save hundreds of dollars during the state's 32-day back-to-school sales tax holiday starting July 20.
cards.body:
Florida families can once again save hundreds of dollars during the state's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday, running from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026. The 32-day tax-free shopping period offers significant savings on essential items families need for the new school year, with no sales tax due on qualifying purchases.

Tax-free items include clothing such as shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear, as well as bags including backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs. School supplies eligible for the exemption include pens, pencils, erasers, notebooks, binders, construction paper, scissors, glue, tape, staplers, lunch boxes and composition books. Learning aids such as flashcards, jigsaw puzzles, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets also qualify. Computers, laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators are included, along with accessories like keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards.

Notable exclusions include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, roller blades and any clothing item over $100. Important price thresholds are $100 per item for clothing and bags, $50 per item for school supplies, $30 per item for learning aids and puzzles, and $1,500 per item for computers and accessories. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption, even if delivered after Aug. 20. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday. All qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period.

hero.body:

He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company.

Rosario Liz credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," Rosario Liz said. He said the club helped him find what his leadership style was going to be and really redefined what his definition of leadership was. "It is such an honor. It has been something so amazing to see how my community sees me as a leader," he said.

He closed with a message for the younger members of the club looking up to him. "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now," Rosario Liz said. The teenager will represent his club and community on the world stage as he carries a flag at one of the most watched sporting events in the world.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November with new renderings released
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium this week, with groundbreaking planned for November and the facility scheduled to open in early 2028.
cards.body:
The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Representatives for Port St. Lucie SC announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction.

The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. The club said the 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity and described it as a year-round gathering place designed for matchdays, concerts, festivals, and community events. Ticket deposits are currently available online. Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said this may be the first cool thing the city has ever actually brought here, though he raised concerns about traffic on U.S. 1. Focus Sanders, a barber at Sapp's Barbershop, said the stadium offers more business because it will bring more people over here. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction.

hero.headline: Indian River County schools develop strategy to reverse enrollment decline amid school choice expansion
hero.body:
Indian River County school officials are working to address enrollment declines as school choice options expand across the county. New research examines the district's strategy for competing in the evolving educational landscape.

The case study explores how district administrators are responding to the challenges posed by expanding school choice programs. Indian River County schools face increasing competition as families gain access to more educational alternatives.

School choice programs have grown significantly in Florida in recent years, allowing parents to direct public education dollars toward charter schools, private schools, and other alternatives to traditional public schools. The expansion has forced traditional school districts to adapt their recruitment and retention strategies.

The research highlights Indian River County's approach as officials work to attract and retain students. District leaders are developing new strategies to compete with alternative education providers as enrollment patterns shift across the county.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
hero.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.
